title: Neuroscience Is Rediscovering an Idea Freud Had 130 Years Ago
hook: Today's leading theory of the brain describes it as a prediction machine constantly guessing what comes next — an idea a new paper says closely echoes psychoanalysis from over a century ago.
key_points: A leading modern brain theory frames the brain as constantly predicting incoming sensations, not just reacting to them.
A new paper argues this closely mirrors ideas Sigmund Freud explored more than 130 years ago.
The comparison is a reframing of intellectual history, not a new experimental result about the brain.
It suggests some psychoanalytic ideas anticipated themes modern neuroscience is now formalizing.
content_html: What if Sigmund Freud was onto something modern neuroscience is only now catching up to? A new paper, covered by ScienceDaily, argues that today's leading theory of the brain — as a "prediction machine" constantly anticipating what it's about to sense rather than just reacting to it — closely mirrors ideas psychoanalysis has explored for more than a century.
extra_html: It's worth being precise about what kind of claim this is: it's an argument about intellectual history and conceptual overlap, not a new experiment proving Freud right. The predictive-brain framework is a genuinely influential idea in contemporary neuroscience, describing perception and even emotion as shaped by the brain's ongoing predictions and how well they match reality. The paper's contribution is pointing out that some of Freud's century-old ideas about unconscious expectation were, in broad strokes, gesturing at similar territory — a reminder that old theories sometimes anticipate the language science eventually catches up with, even when the original framing falls out of favor.

flashcards.back_html: The idea that the brain works mainly by constantly predicting what it's about to sense, rather than passively reacting to the world — a leading framework in modern neuroscience.

flashcards.prompt: What kind of claim is this ScienceDaily piece making?

choices.text: An intellectual-history argument that Freud's ideas anticipated a modern brain theory
A new brain-imaging study proving Freud's theories are literally true
A finding that disproves the predictive-brain theory of neuroscience

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper draws a conceptual parallel between psychoanalysis and today's predictive-brain framework — it's a reframing of ideas, not new experimental evidence.
